questions.question_text: Based on the unseen passage about the healing power of melody, what was the primary effect of the music therapy sessions on the recovering patients?
options: A) It caused them to forget their medical history.
B) It significantly lowered their stress hormones and synchronized their heart rates.
C) It encouraged them to pursue professional careers in classical music.
D) It replaced their need for any physical rehabilitation.
questions.answer: B) It significantly lowered their stress hormones and synchronized their heart rates.

questions.question_text: Which word from the unseen passage is an exact antonym for the word 'aggravate'?
options: A) Intensify
B) Alleviate
C) Provoke
D) Comprehend
questions.answer: B) Alleviate

questions.question_text: According to paragraph three of the passage, the author asserts that rhythm primarily synchronizes with which human biological function?
options: A) The digestive system
B) Visual perception
C) The breathing cycle and heartbeat
D) Muscle growth
questions.answer: C) The breathing cycle and heartbeat

questions.question_text: According to the passage, how does group singing build a sense of community among strangers? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Group singing synchronizes breathing and heart rates among participants. This physical alignment fosters a deep psychological bond, breaking down social barriers and creating a unified, supportive environment where strangers feel an immediate sense of belonging and empathy.

questions.question_text: Identify the reasons the author provides for describing empathy as a 'universal language'. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Empathy transcends spoken languages and cultural boundaries because it relies on shared human emotions. The author explains that expressing genuine compassion through actions or music communicates profound understanding that anyone, regardless of background, can instinctively comprehend and appreciate.

questions.question_text: What final conclusion does the author draw about the necessity of self-belief in personal healing? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The author concludes that while external support like music therapy is beneficial, true recovery requires internal conviction. Individuals must fundamentally believe in their own capacity to heal, transforming passive treatments into active, empowering journeys toward personal restoration.

sections.section_name: Section B - Writing Skills & Applied Grammar

questions.question_text: Identify the option that correctly converts the given active sentence into the Passive Voice: 'The talented musician composed a beautiful symphony for the festival.'
options: A) A beautiful symphony is being composed for the festival by the talented musician.
B) A beautiful symphony had been composed for the festival by the talented musician.
C) A beautiful symphony was composed for the festival by the talented musician.
D) The festival was composed by a beautiful symphony for the talented musician.
questions.answer: C) A beautiful symphony was composed for the festival by the talented musician.

questions.question_text: Identify the option that correctly converts the given passive sentence into the Active Voice: 'The new community library is being built by the local volunteers.'
options: A) The local volunteers built the new community library.
B) The local volunteers are building the new community library.
C) The local volunteers will build the new community library.
D) The local volunteers have been building the new community library.
questions.answer: B) The local volunteers are building the new community library.

questions.question_text: Select the correct indirect speech form for the following sentence: The teacher said to the students, 'Please submit your art projects by tomorrow.'
options: A) The teacher told the students to submit their art projects by tomorrow.
B) The teacher requested the students to submit their art projects by the next day.
C) The teacher said that the students must submit their art projects tomorrow.
D) The teacher ordered the students that they will submit their art projects by the next day.
questions.answer: B) The teacher requested the students to submit their art projects by the next day.

questions.question_text: Select the correct indirect speech form for the following sentence: He asked me, 'Where are you going for the summer vacation?'
options: A) He asked me where I was going for the summer vacation.
B) He asked me where was I going for the summer vacation.
C) He asked me where I am going for the summer vacation.
D) He asked me that where I was going for the summer vacation.
questions.answer: A) He asked me where I was going for the summer vacation.

questions.question_text: Identify the type of subordinate clause in the following sentence: 'The athlete realized that he had to train much harder to win the gold medal.'
options: A) Adjective Clause
B) Adverbial Clause of Time
C) Noun Clause
D) Relative Clause
questions.answer: C) Noun Clause

questions.question_text: Choose the option that correctly combines these sentences using a relative clause: 'The book is very inspiring. I borrowed it from the school library.'
options: A) The book is very inspiring and I borrowed it from the school library.
B) The book which I borrowed from the school library is very inspiring.
C) Because I borrowed the book from the school library, it is very inspiring.
D) The book is very inspiring although I borrowed it from the school library.
questions.answer: B) The book which I borrowed from the school library is very inspiring.

questions.question_text: Identify the correct adverbial clause of condition to complete the sentence: 'You will not be allowed to perform on the main stage ______.'
options: A) until you do not practice your lines.
B) if you do not attend the final dress rehearsal.
C) because you are a good singer.
D) although you arrived on time.
questions.answer: B) if you do not attend the final dress rehearsal.

questions.question_text: Choose the sentence that correctly applies the rules of Subject-Verb concord.
options: A) Neither the principal nor the teachers is attending the morning assembly.
B) Neither the principal nor the teachers are attending the morning assembly.
C) Neither the principal nor the teachers was attending the morning assembly.
D) Neither the principal nor the teachers has attended the morning assembly.
questions.answer: B) Neither the principal nor the teachers are attending the morning assembly.

questions.question_text: Write a short diary entry expressing your feelings after successfully participating in a school musical event despite having initial stage fright. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: Dear Diary, Today was an unforgettable day! I finally performed in the school choir. Before stepping onto the stage, my heart was pounding, and I almost backed out due to intense stage fright. However, the moment the music started, my fears simply melted away. I focused entirely on the rhythm and my fellow singers. The applause at the end felt surreal. I am so proud that I believed in myself and conquered my anxieties. Goodnight!

questions.question_text: Write a formal letter to the Editor of a national daily highlighting the importance of integrating art and music education into the regular school curriculum for holistic student development. [80-100 words]
questions.answer:
To the Editor, The Daily Times.
Subject: Importance of Art and Music in Schools.
Sir/Madam,
Through your esteemed newspaper, I wish to highlight the need to integrate art and music into mainstream education. In our competitive academic environment, students face immense stress. Music and arts provide a crucial creative outlet, fostering emotional intelligence, empathy, and self-expression. They teach discipline and teamwork. A holistic education must nurture both the mind and the soul. I urge educational authorities to make the arts a mandatory part of our schooling system.
Yours sincerely, A Concerned Student.

questions.question_text: Read the extract and identify the correct interpretation: 'He gave out a cry in frustration and anguish / His dreams and his efforts all dashed in the dirt.' (from 'Nine Gold Medals'). What does 'dashed in the dirt' symbolize here?
options: A) His desire to plant a garden in the stadium.
B) His sudden physical injury and the shattering of his lifelong athletic aspirations.
C) His realization that he had brought the wrong shoes for the race.
D) His anger toward the other competitors.
questions.answer: B) His sudden physical injury and the shattering of his lifelong athletic aspirations.

questions.question_text: In the poem 'I Cannot Remember My Mother', what specific sensory imagery does the poet use to evoke the lingering presence of his mother?
options: A) The sound of the temple bells in the evening.
B) The scent of the shiuli flowers in the autumn morning.
C) The sight of rain falling on the green fields.
D) The feeling of a warm blanket on a winter night.
questions.answer: B) The scent of the shiuli flowers in the autumn morning.

questions.question_text: In the story 'A Friend Found in Music', how does the shared passion for melodies serve as a bridge between the two contrasting protagonists? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Despite their contrasting cultural backgrounds and spoken languages, the protagonists find common ground through musical notes. Their shared passion allows them to communicate deep emotions non-verbally, forming a profound and enduring friendship based on mutual artistic respect.

questions.question_text: Explain the central message of empathy depicted in the poem 'Nine Gold Medals' when the athletes turn back. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: When the eight athletes stop and return to help the fallen runner, the poem highlights that human compassion is far more valuable than winning. It redefines true victory as a collective triumph of empathy, solidarity, and sportsmanship.

questions.question_text: According to the chapter 'Canvas of Soil', what deep connection exists between the rural artisan and the natural earth? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The artisan treats the soil not merely as raw material, but as a living canvas holding ancestral memories. The process of shaping the earth represents a sacred, traditional bond, reflecting deep respect for nature and indigenous cultural heritage.

questions.question_text: In the poem 'Words', how does the poet contrast the physical impact of a weapon with the emotional impact of harsh words? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The poet illustrates that while physical weapons leave visible scars that eventually heal, harsh words inflict invisible psychological wounds. These emotional scars linger much longer in the mind, emphasizing the destructive and enduring power of negative language.

questions.question_text: Analyze the transformative journey of the protagonist in 'Believe in Yourself'. How do they overcome their internal doubts to achieve their ultimate goal? [80-100 words]
questions.answer: In 'Believe in Yourself', the protagonist initially struggles with crippling self-doubt and the fear of failure, which acts as their biggest obstacle. The transformation begins when they realize that external validation is fleeting and true strength must come from within. By consciously shifting their mindset, practicing daily affirmations, and embracing small failures as learning opportunities, they slowly build resilience. This internal shift allows them to tune out negative criticism and focus entirely on their passion. Ultimately, their unwavering self-belief becomes the catalyst for their success, proving that confidence and perseverance can conquer any adversity.

questions.question_text: Discuss the themes of dignity of labor and respect for traditional roots as highlighted in 'Gifts of Grace Honouring Our Vocations' and 'Bharat Our Land'. [80-100 words]
questions.answer: Both texts celebrate the inherent dignity and profound value of all forms of work. 'Gifts of Grace Honouring Our Vocations' emphasizes that every profession, whether manual or intellectual, contributes uniquely to society and should be pursued with dedication and pride. It dismantles the hierarchy of labor. Similarly, 'Bharat Our Land' reinforces this by connecting the fruits of labor to the rich, diverse soil of the nation. It instills a deep sense of patriotism and respect for traditional roots, showing that honoring our vocations is ultimately a way of honoring our homeland and its enduring cultural legacy.
